units.en: Yannian, Cang, Gong, and Shou were all enfeoffed as marquises.'
units.literal: Enfeoffed Yannian, Cang, Gong, Shou all as marquises."

units.zh: 文雅雖不能及蕭望之、匡衡，然指意略同。
units.en: His literary polish fell short of Xiao Wangzhi's or Kuang Heng's, but his aims ran along the same lines.
units.literal: In cultured elegance though he could not reach Xiao Wangzhi and Kuang Heng, yet his pointed meaning was broadly the same.

units.zh: 其父睹之，經於溝瀆，亡益救敗，不如趙母指括，以全其宗。
units.en: His father chose suicide in a ditch—a useless gesture beside Zhao Kuo's mother, who denounced her son to save the family.
units.literal: His father saw it and hanged himself in a ditch and drain—no benefit in saving ruin, not equal to Zhao Kuo's mother pointing at Kuo to preserve her clan.

units.zh: 傅喜字稚游，河內溫人也，哀帝祖母定陶傅太后從父弟。
units.en: Fu Xi, courtesy name Zhiyou, came from Wen in Henei commandery. He was a paternal cousin of Grand Empress Dowager Fu of Dingtao, Emperor Ai's grandmother.
units.literal: Fu Xi, courtesy name Zhiyou, was a man of Wen in Henei; he was a younger paternal cousin of Empress Dowager Fu of Dingtao, Emperor Ai's grandmother.

units.zh: 後數月，遂策免喜曰：「君輔政出入三年，未有昭然匡朕不逮，而本朝大臣遂其奸心，咎由君焉。
units.en: Months later an edict stripped him of office: 'You have held power for three years without once plainly correcting my shortcomings, while intriguers in this court have had their way. The blame rests with you.
units.literal: After several months, then by edict he dismissed Xi, saying: 'Lord, in assisting government going in and out three years, there has not been clear correction of Our not reaching, while ministers of this court have accomplished their treacherous hearts—the fault is from the lord.

units.zh: 其上大司馬印綬，就第。」
units.en: Surrender the grand marshal's seal and sash and retire to your estate.'
units.literal: Present the grand marshal's seal and ribbon; go to your mansion.'

units.zh: 後又欲奪喜侯，上亦不聽。
units.en: She later tried to strip him of his title as well, but the emperor would not allow it.
units.literal: Later she again wished to strip Xi of his marquisate; the sovereign also did not listen.

units.zh: 喜在國三歲余，哀帝崩，平帝即位，王莽用事，免傅氏宮爵歸故郡，晏將妻子徙合浦。
units.en: Fu Xi spent three years in his fief. After Emperor Ai died and the child Emperor Ping ascended, Wang Mang took charge, stripped the Fu clan of their titles, and sent them home; Fu Yan removed his wife and children to Hepu on the southern coast.
units.literal: Xi was in his state more than three years; Emperor Ai died; Emperor Ping ascended the throne; Wang Mang handled affairs; the Fu clan's palace ranks were dismissed and they returned to their old commanderies; Yan led wife and children and moved to Hepu.

units.zh: 哀帝立爲太子，成帝選喜爲太子庶子。
units.en: When Emperor Ai was made crown prince, Emperor Cheng appointed Fu Xi palace attendant to the heir.
units.literal: When Emperor Ai was established as heir apparent, Emperor Cheng selected Xi as palace attendant to the heir.

units.zh: 哀帝初即位，以喜爲衛尉，遷右將軍。
units.en: When Emperor Ai first took the throne, Fu Xi was made Commandant of the Guard and then General of the Right.
units.literal: When Emperor Ai first ascended the throne, Xi was made Commandant of the Guard and transferred to General of the Right.

units.zh: 是時，王莽爲大司馬，乞骸骨，避帝外家。
units.en: At that time Wang Mang served as Grand Marshal but asked to retire in order to step aside before the new emperor's maternal relatives.
units.literal: At this time Wang Mang was Grand Marshal, begged for his old bones, and withdrew to avoid the emperor's consort kin.

units.zh: 上既聽莽退，眾庶歸望於喜。
units.en: Once the emperor accepted Wang Mang's retirement, public expectation turned to Fu Xi.
units.literal: Once the sovereign had heard Mang withdraw, the multitude turned their hopes to Xi.

units.zh: 又帝舅陽安侯丁明，皆親以外屬封。
units.en: The emperor's maternal uncle, Marquis of Yang'an Ding Ming, was likewise enfeoffed as a close maternal relative.
units.literal: Moreover the emperor's maternal uncle Yang'an Marquis Ding Ming—all were close and enfeoffed as outer kin.

units.zh: 上於是用左將軍師丹代王莽爲大司馬，賜喜黃金百斤、上將軍印綬，以光祿大夫養病。
units.en: The emperor then replaced Wang Mang with General of the Left Shi Dan as Grand Marshal, gave Fu Xi one hundred jin of gold and the seal and sash of Upper General, and allowed him to convalesce with the rank of Grand Master of the Household.
units.literal: The sovereign thereupon used General of the Left Shi Dan to replace Wang Mang as Grand Marshal; he bestowed on Xi one hundred jin of gold and the seal and ribbon of the Upper General, and had him nurse illness as Grand Master of the Household.

units.zh: 大司空何武、尚書令唐林皆上書言：「喜行義修潔，忠誠憂國，內輔之臣也，今以寢病，一旦遣歸，眾庶失望，皆曰傅氏賢子，以論議不合於定陶太后故退，百寮莫不為國恨之。
units.en: Grand Minister of Works He Wu and Secretary Director Tang Lin jointly wrote: 'Fu Xi is upright, scrupulous, and devoted to the state—exactly the kind of man who should stand at the emperor's side. To dismiss him overnight on grounds of illness will disappoint the empire. People will say the worthy son of the Fu clan was cashiered because he would not trim his opinions to suit the Dowager of Dingtao, and every official will feel the dynasty has wronged itself.
units.literal: Grand Minister of Works He Wu and secretary director Tang Lin both submitted memorials saying: 'Xi in conduct and righteousness is cultivated and pure, loyal and sincere, worrying for the state; he is a minister of inner assistance; now because of lying illness, in one morning sent back, the multitude will be disappointed; all will say the Fu family's worthy son, because discussions did not accord with the Dowager of Dingtao therefore retired; the hundred officials none do not for the state resent it.

units.zh: 喜立於朝，陛下之光輝，傅氏之廢興也。」
units.en: Fu Xi's presence at court is both your majesty's good fortune and the making or breaking of the Fu clan.'
units.literal: Xi standing at court is Your Majesty's glory and brightness, and the Fu family's ruin or rise.'

units.zh: 上亦自重之。
units.en: The emperor himself still set great store by him.
units.literal: The sovereign also on his own valued him.

units.zh: 明年正月，乃徙師丹為大司空，而拜喜為大司馬，封高武侯。
units.en: The following first month the emperor moved Shi Dan into the grand minister of works post, appointed Fu Xi grand marshal, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Gaowu.
units.literal: In the first month of the next year, Shi Dan was transferred to the office of grand minister of works, and Xi was appointed grand marshal and enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaowu.

units.zh: 傅太后大怒，上不得已，先免師丹以感動喜，喜終不順。
units.en: The grand empress dowager raged. Cornered, the emperor first dismissed Shi Dan, hoping to intimidate Fu Xi into yielding; Fu Xi still refused to bend.
units.literal: The Fu empress dowager was greatly angry; the sovereign had no choice; first he dismissed Shi Dan in order to move Xi; Xi in the end did not comply.

units.zh: 傅太后又自詔丞相、御史曰：「高武侯喜無功而封，內懷不忠，附下罔上，與故大司空丹同心背畔，放命圮族，虧損德化，罪惡雖在赦前，不宜奉朝請，其遣就國。」
units.en: Grand Empress Dowager Fu then issued her own order to the chancellor and censor: 'Marquis of Gaowu Fu Xi received a fief without merit. In his heart he is disloyal: he panders to factions below while misleading the throne, and he conspired with the former grand minister of works Shi Dan in mutinous defiance. Such conduct tears down the moral order. Even though his offenses predate the last amnesty, he must not continue at court; send him back to his fief.'
units.literal: The Fu empress dowager again herself issued an edict the chancellor and imperial secretary, saying: 'Gaowu Marquis Xi was enfeoffed without merit; within he harbors disloyalty, attaches to those below and deceives those above; with the former grand minister of works Dan of one mind he turned his back and rebelled; he abandoned commands and ruined the clan; he damaged and diminished virtuous transformation; although crimes and evils were before the amnesty, it is not fitting that he attend court audience; let him be sent to his state.'

units.zh: 贊曰：自宜、元、成、哀外戚興者，許、史、三王、丁、傅之家，皆重侯累將，窮貴極富，見其位矣，未見其人也。
units.en: The historian's judgment: From the reigns of Xuan through Ai, the consort clans—the Xu, the Shi, the three Wang lines, the Ding, and the Fu—stacked marquisates and generalships until they towered in wealth and rank; you could see their offices, rarely the men who deserved them.
units.literal: The appraiser says: From Emperor Xuan, Yuan, Cheng, and Ai, those by whom outer kin rose—the houses of Xu, Shi, the three Wangs, Ding, and Fu—all piled marquisates and repeated generalships, exhausted nobility and exhausted wealth; one sees their positions, one has not seen their persons.

units.zh: 哀、平際會，禍福速哉！
units.en: How swiftly fortune and misfortune alternated at the juncture of the Ai and Ping reigns!
units.literal: At the juncture meeting of Ai and Ping—misfortune and fortune swift!

units.zh: 秋，使護西域騎都尉甘延壽、副校尉陳湯撟發戊己校尉屯田吏士及西域胡兵攻郅支單于。
units.en: In autumn, Protector of the Western Regions and Cavalry Commandant Gan Yanshou and Vice Commandant Chen Tang were sent to mobilize the Wuji Commandant's garrison farming officials and soldiers, as well as Western Regions Hu troops, to attack Chanyu Zhizhi.
units.literal: Autumn, sent Protector Western Regions Cavalry Commandant Gan Yanshou, Vice Commandant Chen Tang mobilized Wuji Commandant garrison farming officials soldiers and Western Regions Hu troops attacked Zhizhi Chanyu.

units.zh: 夏，封騎都尉甘延壽為列侯。
units.en: In summer, Cavalry Commandant Gan Yanshou was enfeoffed as a marquis.
units.literal: Summer, enfeoffed Cavalry Commandant Gan Yanshou as marquis.

units.zh: 冬，斬其首，傳詣京師，縣蠻夷邸門。
units.en: In winter, his head was beheaded, transmitted to the capital, and hung on the barbarian residence gate.
units.literal: Winter, beheaded his head, transmitted to capital, hung barbarian barbarian residence gate.

units.zh: 是後，所言益不用，豐復上書言：「臣聞伯奇孝而棄於親，子胥忠而誅於君，隱公慈而殺於弟，叔武弟而殺于兄。
units.en: Feng again submitted a memorial saying, "I have heard that Boqi was filial yet cast off by kin, Wu Zixu loyal yet executed by his ruler, Duke Yin merciful yet killed by his younger brother, and Shuwu the younger brother yet killed by his elder brother.
units.literal: Afterward his words were ever less heeded; Feng again submitted a memorial saying, "I have heard that Boqi was filial yet cast off by kin, Wu Zixu loyal yet executed by his ruler, Duke Yin merciful yet killed by his younger brother, and Shuwu the younger brother yet killed by his elder brother.

units.zh: 大將軍光秉政，領尚書事，車騎將軍金日磾、左將軍上官桀副焉。
units.en: Grand General Guang held the government, led the Secretariat affairs, with Chariot Cavalry General Jin Midi and Left General Shangguan Jie as his assistants.
units.literal: Grand general Guang held government, led Secretariat affairs, Chariot Cavalry General Jin Midi, Left General Shangguan Jie assisted.

units.zh: 發軍屯西河，左將軍桀行北邊。
units.en: Troops were dispatched to garrison Xihe commandery, and General of the Left Shangguan Jie inspected the northern frontier.
units.literal: Troops were dispatched to garrison Xihe; General of the Left Jie patrolled the northern frontier.

units.zh: 二年春正月，大將軍光、左將軍桀皆以前捕斬反虜重合侯馬通功封，光為博陸侯，桀為安陽侯。
units.en: In the first month of spring of the second year, Grand General Huo Guang and Left General Shangguan Jie were both enfeoffed for their previous merit in capturing and executing the rebel bandit Marquis Ma Tong of Chonghe. Guang became Marquis of Bolu, Jie became Marquis of Anyang.
units.literal: Second year spring first month, grand general Guang, left general Jie all with previous capture behead rebel bandits Chonghe marquis Ma Tong merit enfeoffed, Guang as Bolu marquis, Jie as Anyang marquis.

units.zh: 九月，鄂邑長公主、燕王旦與左將軍上官桀、桀子票騎將軍安、御史大夫桑弘羊皆謀反，伏誅。
units.en: In the ninth month, the Elder Princess of Eyi, King Dan of Yan, Left General Shangguan Jie, Jie's son Flying Cavalry General An, and Imperial Secretary Sang Hongyang all plotted rebellion and were executed.
units.literal: Ninth month, Eyi Elder Princess, Yan King Dan with Left General Shangguan Jie, Jie son Flying Cavalry General An, Imperial Secretary Sang Hongyang all plotted rebellion, suffered execution.

units.zh: 初，桀、 安父子與大將軍光爭權，欲害之，詐使人為燕王旦上書言光罪。
units.en: Initially, Shangguan Jie and his son An contended for power with Grand General Huo Guang and wished to harm him. They falsely had someone submit a memorial in the name of King Dan of Yan accusing Guang of crimes.
units.literal: Initially, Jie, An father son with Grand General Guang contended power, wished to harm him, falsely made person for Yan King Dan memorial speak Guang crimes.

units.zh: 冬十月，詔曰：「左將軍安陽侯桀、票騎將軍桑樂侯安、御史大夫弘羊皆數以邪枉干輔政，大將軍不聽， 而懷怨望，與燕王通謀，置驛往來相約結。
units.en: In the tenth month of winter, an edict stated: 'Left General Marquis Jie of Anyang, Flying Cavalry General Marquis An of Sang Le, and Imperial Secretary Hongyang all repeatedly interfered in the auxiliary government with crooked and perverse actions. The Grand General would not listen, so they harbored resentment and communicated with King Yan in plotting, establishing post stations for coming and going and mutually agreeing to join together.
units.literal: Winter tenth month, edict said: Left general Anyang marquis Jie, flying cavalry general Sang Le marquis An, imperial secretary Hongyang all repeatedly with crooked perverse interfered auxiliary government, grand general not listen, and harbored resentment, with Yan King communicated plotted, established post stations come go mutually agreed joined.

units.zh: 又曰：「燕王迷惑失道，前與齊王子劉澤等為逆，抑而不揚，望王反道自新，今乃與長公主及左將軍 桀等謀危宗廟。
units.en: The edict continued: 'The King of Yan was confused and lost his way. He had previously joined Prince Liu Ze of Qi and others in rebellion. Though this was suppressed and not widely publicized in the hope that the king would reform and return to the proper path, he has now conspired with the Long Princess and General of the Left Jie to endanger the ancestral temples.
units.literal: Further said: 'Yan King was confused and lost the Way, previously with Qi Prince Liu Ze and others committed rebellion, suppressed and not raised, hoped King would return to Way and renew himself, now instead with Long Princess and General of the Left Jie and others plotted to endanger ancestral temple.

units.zh: 其赦王太子建、公主子文信及宗室子與燕王、上官桀等謀反父母同產當坐者，皆免為庶人。
units.en: The king's heir apparent Jian, the princess's son Wenxin, and the imperial clansmen who had plotted rebellion with the King of Yan and Shangguan Jie, together with their parents and full siblings who would normally be implicated, were all pardoned and reduced to commoner status.
units.literal: Pardon the king's heir apparent Jian, the princess's son Wenxin, and the imperial clansmen who with the King of Yan and Shangguan Jie and others plotted rebellion, and their parents and full siblings who should be implicated—all reduce to commoners.

units.zh: 其吏為桀等所詿誤，未發覺在吏者， 除其罪。」
units.en: The officials who had been deceived and misled by Jie and his confederates, and whose involvement had not yet been discovered while they remained in office, were pardoned of their crimes."
units.literal: Their officials who were deceived and misled by Jie and others, not yet discovered while in office, remove their crimes."

units.zh: 孝昭幼年即位，亦有燕、盍、上官逆亂之謀。
units.en: When Emperor Zhao the Filial ascended the throne in his youth, there were likewise conspiracies of rebellion involving King Yan, the Elder Princess, and the Shangguan faction.
units.literal: Emperor Zhao the Filial ascended the throne in his youth, and likewise there were plots of rebellion by Yan, Gai, and Shangguan.
